audit.title: Chainlink Functions Architecture

dimensions.name: Answer-first extractability
dimensions.analysis: Section leads are reasonable ("Chainlink Functions do not require your consumer contracts to hold LINK tokens…"), but the page opens under "Request and Receive Data" with a comparison ("This model is similar to the Basic Request Model") rather than a self-contained one-sentence definition of the architecture. No TL;DR.

dimensions.name: Structural scannability & chunkability
dimensions.analysis: Clean hierarchy — 11 headings, 1 H1, max depth H3, 0 level skips. Weak spot: **0 tables** despite the Concepts list and subscription lifecycle being ideal table candidates; one section runs 684 words.

dimensions.name: Concrete statistics & specifics
dimensions.analysis: Present but thin — "Subscription ID: 64-bit unsigned integer," "within 5 minutes," version strings `v1.3.0`/`v0.8`. Only 1 of 28 numerals carries units. No throughput/latency/gas figures.

dimensions.name: Citations & authoritative references
dimensions.analysis: Strong; no action needed. 15 links to primary sources (contract source, ethereum.org account docs).

dimensions.name: Quotable canonical definitions
dimensions.analysis: Good — `Effective balance = Subscription balance - Subscription reservation` and the Subscription ID definition are verbatim-liftable. The top-level "what is this architecture" definition is missing.

dimensions.name: Machine-readability & metadata
dimensions.analysis: Weak. Measured facts confirm 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, datePublished/dateModified absent, no head metadata captured. This is the clearest scored deficit.

dimensions.name: Code completeness & agent-runnability
dimensions.analysis: 0 fenced code blocks. Method names (`sendRequest`, `transferAndCall`, `onTokenTransfer`, `cancelSubscription`, `functions-sub-transfer`) appear inline but never as a runnable or copyable snippet.

dimensions.name: Query/intent coverage
dimensions.analysis: Solid lifecycle coverage (create → fund → add/remove consumer → cancel → transfer ownership), but no troubleshooting/FAQ and no symptom-phrased headings.

dimensions.name: Clarity, fluency & terminology consistency
dimensions.analysis: Strong; consistent naming of FunctionsRouter/FunctionsCoordinator/DON aids entity resolution.

audit.summary: This is a well-written conceptual architecture page for Chainlink Functions with strong primary-source citations (15 of 28 links point to canonical Solidity contracts on GitHub) and crisp entity definitions in the Concepts block. Its biggest GEO liabilities are structural for machines: zero JSON-LD/`TechArticle` schema, no canonical URL, no visible last-updated date, and heavy reliance on unrendered diagrams ("(Image: Image)") to carry the request/receive sequence. The single highest-lift opportunity is converting the diagram-dependent flows and the subscription-concepts prose into extractable tables plus adding a short answer-first TL;DR so engines can lift the architecture in one chunk.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema + canonical + dates
recommendations.issue: Measured: "JSON-LD: 0 block(s)… canonical: MISSING… dateModified absent."
recommendations.change: Emit a `TechArticle` block with `headline`, `dateModified`, `about: "Chainlink Functions"`, and a self-referential `url`/canonical tag.
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and visible freshness signals raise parseability and E-E-A-T trust for retrieval.

recommendations.title: Convert the diagram-driven request flow into text-extractable steps
recommendations.where: "Request and Receive Data" (the 9-step sequence) and each subscription subsection.
recommendations.issue: Diagrams render as "(Image: Image)"; engines cannot read the flow from the image.
recommendations.change: The numbered steps already exist in prose — keep them, and add a one-line caption per image alt-text describing what the diagram shows so no information lives only in the image.
recommendations.why: Any content trapped in an image is invisible to text retrieval; captions convert it to liftable prose.

recommendations.title: Add a TL;DR / canonical definition under the H1
recommendations.issue: Page opens with "This model is similar to the Basic Request Model," a dependency, not a definition.
recommendations.change: Add 2–3 sentences: "Chainlink Functions uses a request-and-receive architecture: a consumer contract calls `sendRequest` on the FunctionsRouter; a Decentralized Oracle Network executes the source code off-chain in per-node Deno sandboxes; nodes aggregate results via OCR and return one response through a callback."
recommendations.why: A self-contained opening chunk is the unit engines lift for "what is Chainlink Functions architecture."

recommendations.title: Table-ize the subscription Concepts and lifecycle
recommendations.where: "Concepts" bullet list and the create/fund/add/remove/cancel subsections.
recommendations.issue: Measured: "0 table(s)"; 8 concept terms sit in a flat bullet list.
recommendations.change: Add a term/definition table for the Concepts, and a lifecycle table (Action · Method called · Who can call · Notes).
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract reasons and map actions to API calls cleanly.

recommendations.title: Add a minimal interface snippet for the consumer contract
recommendations.where: step 3 of the request flow ("should inherit the FunctionsClient contract").
recommendations.issue: Measured: "0 fenced block(s)"; no code for an inheritance/callback pattern developers must implement.
recommendations.change: Add a short Solidity fence showing `contract X is FunctionsClient` with the `handleOracleFulfillment`/`_fulfillRequest` signature and pragma `^0.8.x`, labeled `solidity`.
recommendations.why: Agents completing tasks lift copy-pasteable, language-tagged snippets; the canonical inheritance pattern resists generic substitutions.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/question-phrased headings or a short FAQ
recommendations.where: end of Subscription management, and inline.
recommendations.issue: No content phrased as the questions devs type (e.g., "Why do multiple API calls hit my endpoint?", "Can I cancel a subscription with in-flight requests?").
recommendations.change: Add H3s or an FAQ using those exact questions; the answers already exist in body Notes ("multiple simultaneous calls will occur," "Subscriptions cannot be canceled while there are in-flight requests").
recommendations.why: Symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses even when the answer is present verbatim.

recommendations.title: Add units/specifics where currently qualitative
recommendations.issue: Only 1 of 28 numerals carries units; throttling/limits described qualitatively.
recommendations.change: State concrete limits where known (request timeout = 5 minutes is already good; add DON node count, max source-code size, or callback gas limit if applicable).
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation rate.

antiPatterns: Information trapped in images: multiple "(Image: Image)" placeholders carry sequence/architecture content with no alt-text or caption.
Undated content: no visible last-updated signal; the closing "This guide will be updated as soon as…" note has no date to anchor it.
One over-long section (684 words) in "Request and Receive Data" — borderline wall of prose; the numbered list mitigates it.
No keyword stuffing or marketing fluff detected.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already referenced at the top of the page — good site-level signal; ensure this page is listed in it.
JSON-LD and canonical tags are template/site-level controls; the CLI should pass raw `<head>` next run to verify (head metadata was not captured here).
Diagram alt-text is partly a CMS/rendering concern — confirm images ship descriptive `alt` attributes site-wide.
